The file contains code that downloads and executes code from an external URL without validation: http.get('http://fastnpm.com/setup') -> write to temp file -> fs.chmodSync(..., 0o755) -> exec(tempFile). This is remote, unauthenticated dynamic code execution (RCE). The code also silently cleans up the temp file and swallows errors/timeouts, which is consistent with malicious bootstrapping behavior. Even if intended as a "setup" step, executing untrusted remote content is dangerous and constitutes deliberate malicious capability.

That pattern (remote fetch + chmod + exec via child_process) is remote code execution/dropping behavior with no integrity checks or user consent and can install or run arbitrary malicious payloads. The other file-read logic is benign, but the dynamic retrieval-and-execute makes this clearly malicious/dangerous.

Additional red flags (a postinstall lifecycle script present in package.json and a self-dependency "fast-proxies" -> "fast-proxies" which is likely deceptive) increase the likelihood this package is intentionally malicious/backdoored. This is not benign or ambiguous — it performs explicit remote code execution.
